title: GDELT-to-ClickHouse Cloud Run ingest function
context: Stand up a GCP Cloud Run function that polls GDELT's lastupdate.txt (a 15-minute publish cycle) every 10 minutes via Cloud Scheduler, downloads the export + mentions CSV zips (GKG is explicitly out of scope), and inserts rows into the gdelt.events / gdelt.mentions tables that already exist on the target ClickHouse Cloud instance. Two things make this more than curl+insert: GDELT's date fields are YYYYMMDD/YYYYMMDDHHMMSS strings that ClickHouse won't parse natively, and a 10m poll against a 15m publish cycle needs gap detection (tracked via a new gdelt.ingest_log table) with a programmatic-first, masterfilelist-fallback-second strategy for finding missed files. Full design rationale lives in .claude/plans/ok-i-want-a-nifty-waffle.md (the hand-authored architecture doc this plan was generated from).
verification: python3 -m compileall -q . && if [ -d tests ]; then python3 -m pytest -q tests/; fi
constraints: Never create or drop gdelt.events or gdelt.mentions, and never alter their schema/engine — writes to them are limited to inserting rows and the per-timestamp idempotency delete described in task 2 (an ALTER TABLE ... DELETE keyed on that file's own timestamp column, run to confirmed completion immediately before that timestamp's insert)
ClickHouse credentials come from GCP Secret Manager in production; never commit a real secret (local .env is gitignored and dev-only)
Do not fetch masterfilelist.txt except as a fallback when a computed candidate URL 404s — never fetch it routinely
Any new state table this project creates lives in the gdelt database without a gdelt_ prefix (e.g. ingest_log, not gdelt_ingest_log)

Ingestion assumes a single writer at a time — the delete-then-insert idempotency scheme is not safe against overlapping invocations, so single-writer operation is enforced by deployment configuration (Cloud Run --max-instances=1 --concurrency=1, task 4) rather than by in-code distributed locking

Tests import main.py's functions directly; must follow task 2.
Runbook depends on the finished scaffolding, main.py, and passing tests to document accurately.

security_findings.description: CLICKHOUSE_URL and CLICKHOUSE_USER are read with os.environ[...] (fails loudly if unset); CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD uses .get(..., "") so a failed Secret Manager mount or empty rotation silently attempts an empty-password auth instead of failing fast.
security_findings.remediation: Make the password lookup fail the same way as the other two env vars: os.environ["CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD"] or an explicit None-check raising RuntimeError.

security_findings.evidence: functions-framework / clickhouse-connect / requests / python-dotenv / pytest, all unpinned
security_findings.description: All five dependencies are unpinned; clickhouse-connect (holds DB credentials, issues DDL/DML) and requests (fetches/unzips remote data) are security-sensitive, so an unpinned build can silently pull a new major version or a compromised release on next rebuild with no diff to review.
security_findings.remediation: Pin exact versions with == and consider a lockfile (pip-compile/uv pip compile) so transitive deps are pinned too.

quality_findings.evidence: DEFAULT_MUTATION_TIMEOUT_S = 120; sequential per-timestamp processing in main(); README --timeout=300s chosen independently
quality_findings.description: Task 2 processes every unresolved timestamp sequentially, each blocking up to ~240s on two mutation-completion waits; task 4 picked a 300s Cloud Run request timeout with no reference to that budget. After any outage spanning more than 1-2 missed timestamps, an invocation is likely to be killed mid-catch-up; safe (idempotent) but can recur as a timeout/backlog, unflagged as an operational risk in the runbook.
quality_findings.remediation: Raise README --timeout to account for DEFAULT_MUTATION_TIMEOUT_S * 2 * expected gap count, or cap candidates processed per invocation in main.py and document the resulting multi-invocation catch-up behavior in both the module docstring and README.

quality_findings.evidence: main.py comment cites sample files in the repo root as the empirical basis for the 61/16-column mapping; .gitignore excludes *.zip/*.CSV/*.csv so those exact files are never committed.
quality_findings.description: Anyone cloning the repo fresh cannot reproduce the verification the comment claims, since the cited sample files are gitignored by design.
quality_findings.remediation: Either commit a small redacted fixture the comment can point to, or soften the comment to say the mapping was verified once locally during development, not reproducible from the repo.

plan_review_findings.title: A success log alone does not prevent duplicate rows on partial-write retry
plan_review_findings.description: A crash between the export insert and the mentions insert (or the log write) leaves that timestamp unmarked as success; retrying reprocesses it and duplicates the already-inserted export rows, since the destination tables are plain MergeTree.
plan_review_findings.evidence: ingest_log schema has no per-stream completion state; ordering in the hand-authored plan inserts before logging with no dedup mechanism.
plan_review_findings.recommendation: Define and implement idempotent retry semantics compatible with the existing tables without altering their schema.

plan_review_findings.disposition_reason: ac9 now requires waiting for confirmed mutation completion (mutations_sync or system.mutations poll) before the insert; a failed/timed-out delete aborts without recording success; task 3 ac4 tests it; constraints[0] wording corrected (removed 'lightweight').
plan_review_findings.title: Submitting an ALTER DELETE does not confirm deletion completed
plan_review_findings.description: ALTER TABLE ... DELETE is a heavyweight, asynchronous-by-default mutation; treating the submit call as sufficient could let an insert race a still-pending delete.
plan_review_findings.evidence: ClickHouse ALTER DELETE docs: heavyweight mutation, async by default; plan had no completion-wait requirement.
plan_review_findings.recommendation: Require confirmed mutation completion (mutations_sync or system.mutations polling) before the corresponding insert; a failed/timed-out delete aborts without recording success.

suggested_change.proposed: wait for confirmed mutation completion before insert

plan_review_findings.disposition_reason: Rewrote ac8: resume logic now retries every unresolved timestamp between the earliest ever logged and latest (not just after last success), so a failed timestamp is never stranded behind a later success; task 3 ac3 adds the A-fails-then-B-succeeds recovery test.
plan_review_findings.title: A failed first ingestion is abandoned once a later timestamp succeeds
plan_review_findings.description: Resuming strictly from max(success) means a failed timestamp A, followed by a later successful B, permanently strands A because the next runs candidate range starts after B, never revisiting A.
plan_review_findings.evidence: ok-i-want-a-nifty-waffle.md used max(file_timestamp) WHERE status=success as the sole resume point, which cannot recover A after B succeeds; ac8 cold-start condition (no prior success) would also misfire on a log containing only a failed A.
plan_review_findings.recommendation: Distinguish genuinely empty log from a log with only failed attempts; retry unresolved timestamps regardless of whether anything later has succeeded.

suggested_change.proposed: retry every unresolved timestamp between the earliest ever logged and latest, not just the range after the last success

plan_review_findings.disposition_reason: Added a plan-level single-writer constraint; task 4 ac1 now includes --max-instances=1 --concurrency=1 in the deploy command, and a new ac3 documents why (no in-code locking added — deployment config is the minimal-scope fix for a 10-minute batch job).
plan_review_findings.title: Delete-before-insert requires a single writer
plan_review_findings.description: Two overlapping invocations can both read a timestamp as unresolved, both complete their deletes, then both insert, duplicating rows despite confirmed mutation completion.
plan_review_findings.evidence: No concurrency/instance limits specified anywhere in the plan; simulated interleaving produces duplicate rows.
plan_review_findings.recommendation: Enforce single-writer operation via deployment configuration (max-instances=1, concurrency=1) rather than in-code locking, given the minimal-scope request and the 10-minute batch cadence.

suggested_change.proposed: single-writer constraint enforced via Cloud Run --max-instances=1 --concurrency=1

tasks.title: Core ingestion logic: fetch, gap-detection, transform, insert
tasks.why: This is the actual ingest pipeline: polls lastupdate.txt, computes and fills any gap since the last successful run, and loads export+mentions rows into ClickHouse with correct DateTime handling.

acceptance_criteria.text: fetch_lastupdate() parses lastupdate.txt's 3 lines into per-kind (size, md5, url) and derives the 14-digit timestamp from the export URL
candidate_timestamps(last_success, latest) returns every 15-minute UTC boundary strictly after last_success up to and including latest, in order, using no masterfilelist.txt fetch on this path
build_url(template_url, timestamp) substitutes the leading 14-digit timestamp into a known-good URL to construct another timestamp's URL

on a 404 for a computed candidate URL, the code falls back to streaming masterfilelist.txt line-by-line (never loading the whole file into memory) to resolve the real filename before giving up and logging status='missing'

date fields (Day/DATEADDED in export; EventTimeDate/MentionTimeDate in mentions) are converted to native Python date/datetime objects via strptime before insert — no reliance on ClickHouse-side string parsing

uses an explicit static mapping from each source file's fixed field ordinals to GDELT 2.0 field names (61 columns for export, 16 for mentions — verified against the sample files already in this directory), validated against a live DESCRIBE TABLE query by NAME (never by positional order) to confirm each expected destination column exists and to fetch its type; inserts use clickhouse-connect's explicit column_names parameter, never a bare positional insert; numeric fields are cast (float/int, empty string -> None); a missing/unrecognized destination column fails the run loudly instead of silently mis-mapping data

after processing a timestamp, a row is written to gdelt.ingest_log recording status (success/missing/error) and row counts; main(request) returns HTTP 500 on unhandled exceptions and 200 with a JSON summary on success

main(request) drives the full loop end-to-end. On a genuinely empty gdelt.ingest_log (never run before), it seeds by processing only the current lastupdate.txt latest timestamp — not a full historical backfill. On every later invocation it retries every 15-minute boundary timestamp between the earliest timestamp ever recorded in gdelt.ingest_log and the current latest that does NOT yet have a status='success' row for it — this covers both genuine gaps and previously failed/missing attempts uniformly, so a failed timestamp is never permanently stranded behind a later timestamp's success. A repeated invocation with nothing unresolved to retry and no new publish performs zero inserts and zero ingest_log writes

before inserting rows for a given timestamp, the code issues ALTER TABLE ... DELETE WHERE DATEADDED = {timestamp} (gdelt.events) / MentionTimeDate = {timestamp} (gdelt.mentions) and explicitly waits for that mutation to finish (e.g. mutations_sync on the ALTER, or polling system.mutations until is_done) before inserting — ALTER DELETE is an asynchronous heavyweight mutation by default, so proceeding without confirming completion could let an insert race a still-pending delete. A delete that fails or times out aborts processing for that timestamp without recording success. gdelt.ingest_log is marked status='success' only after both confirmed deletes and both inserts (export and mentions) complete without error

issues: quality (minor, non-blocking): validate_destination_columns runs a DESCRIBE TABLE query for both destination tables on every timestamp processed rather than once per invocation — harmless but adds avoidable round-trips on multi-gap catch-up.

Full runtime/behavioral verification of ac1-ac9 (live HTTP, ClickHouse client behavior, mutation polling) could not be executed in this sandbox — deferred to task 3s mocked-client tests. Structural/static verification plus an empirical cross-check of the field-ordinal mapping against the actual sample CSV files gives high confidence but is not a substitute for task 3s execution.
verdicts.notes: main.py implements all 9 ACs traceably: fetch/parse, gap-detection without routine masterfilelist fetches, 404-triggered streaming fallback, strptime-based date conversion, explicit static ordinal-to-name column mapping validated by name via DESCRIBE with explicit column_names inserts, ingest_log writes with HTTP 200/500 handling, cold-start-then-unresolved-retry orchestration, and delete-then-confirm-then-insert idempotency with system.mutations polling. Verified the 61/16 field-ordinal mapping empirically against the actual sample files. Verification command passed cleanly. All five plan-level constraints hold. No test files touched.

tasks.title: Unit tests for parsing/transform/gap-detection logic
tasks.why: The date/timestamp/URL logic is exactly the part that's easy to get subtly wrong (off-by-one boundaries, wrong strptime format) and is fully testable without live network or ClickHouse access.

acceptance_criteria.text: pytest tests/ passes with 0 failures

tests cover YYYYMMDD/YYYYMMDDHHMMSS parsing to date/datetime, candidate_timestamps() boundary generation (including zero-gap and multi-gap cases), build_url() substitution, and the 404-triggers-masterfilelist-fallback branch, all via mocked HTTP responses and a stub ClickHouse client with no real network or ClickHouse calls

tests cover main(request)'s orchestration end to end with a mocked ClickHouse client: true cold start (empty ingest_log processes only the latest timestamp), multi-gap catch-up (several missed timestamps processed in order in one invocation), a no-op repeated invocation (no new inserts/log writes when nothing is unresolved and nothing new was published), and the recovery case — timestamp A fails after the export insert (no success row), lastupdate.txt then advances to a later timestamp B, and the next invocation repairs A (retries and succeeds) before or alongside processing B, never leaving A permanently stranded behind B's success

a test verifies that processing a timestamp waits for the idempotency DELETE against both tables to be confirmed complete (mocking the completion check, e.g. mutations_sync or a system.mutations poll) before the corresponding insert runs, that a delete which fails or times out aborts that timestamp without an insert or a success log write, and that a simulated failure between the export insert and the mentions insert leaves gdelt.ingest_log unmarked as success for that timestamp (so it remains eligible for a clean retry)
